title: Fetch API in Next.js
definition: Next.js drastically extends the native Web `fetch()` API, adding caching and revalidation logic directly into the function call.
simpleExplanation: In React, `fetch` just grabs data. In Next.js, `fetch` is magical. It remembers the data it fetched. If 1,000 users visit your page, Next.js only runs `fetch` once, caches the result on the server, and instantly serves that cached result to all 1,000 users.
realWorldExample: Fetching a list of blog posts from a headless CMS. You want it to be incredibly fast, so you use Next.js `fetch` to cache the response indefinitely.

basic: Does Next.js cache `fetch` requests by default?
intermediate: If you are using a third-party database library (like Prisma or Mongoose) instead of `fetch`, does Next.js automatically cache it?

answers.question: Cached by default?
answers.answer: Yes! In the App Router, any standard `fetch` call is automatically cached (acting like Static Site Generation) unless you specifically tell it not to.

answers.question: Does Prisma cache?
answers.answer: No. Next.js ONLY patches the native `fetch` function. If you use an ORM like Prisma or a library like Axios, it will NOT be cached automatically by the Next.js Data Cache. You must use the `unstable_cache` function to cache DB queries manually.
